segments.text: And once again, same iteration, 4 equals 4 plus itself.
So, Vii would be 8, but I don't think there's any way to get 8 on the left side of the equation.
And if I move the vertical one in the V to the left side of the equation, that becomes 9 equals 4 plus 4.
That still doesn't add correctly either.
Let's see if it was 6 minus 3, but I don't think that would work either.
And if I move the right side of the equation, one of the slanted matchsticks in the Vs, it just becomes IX, which is 9 plus 4 makes the number even higher.
Um, just switching the eye on the left side of the equation doesn't work either.
Because then that 6 equals 4 plus 4, that is incorrect.
9 equals 4 plus 4 is about the closest I can get, but I know that isn't correct, so not sure which one to swap.
Then once again, changing the addition symbol to subtraction I don't think works either, because then what do you do with only the horizontal one?
So I think that's meant to stay.

Once again, the easiest solution would just be to move one of the vertical, er, slanted matchsticks, rather, directly through the equals sign so that 4 does not equal 4, I don't know, 4 plus 2, even though the slanted and the exactly vertical sticks aren't the same.
